edit.description: the run schema asks the forge for the run's own commit, the tip read resolves the tip's sha, and the staleness refusal compares the two naming both; `commitInstantAt` and the ISO `instant` parse leave with the ordering they served
the run render names the run's own commit, the fact the block now states beside the id and the conclusion
both arms of the swap, beside the existing staleness cases

summary: A lane read orders created instants, so an amended tip or a re-run of an older run reads another tree's run as this tip's — the forge states the run's own commit outright

per.section: CI lanes as a findings source

acceptance: a lane's newest completed run is this tip's evidence exactly when the run's own commit is the tip, and reads `UNREAD` naming both commits otherwise — so the render's block and the stamp-bearing run report the run's commit rather than its created instant, and the tip-instant read and its offset parse leave with the comparison they served
tests: a lane read refuses a run whose own commit is not the tip's
a lane read gives a verdict off the tip's own run whatever instant the forge created it at
notes: Drains the ruling on `questions/is-a-lane-read-refused-by-the-runs-own-sha-rather-than-its-instant.md`, fork (A); closed here. Verified on disk: `behindTheTip` (`harness/ci.ts:591`) orders `instant(run.at)` against `instant(tip.at)`; `RUN_FIELDS` (`:181`) is derived from `RunSchema`'s keys, so asking for `headSha` is one field. The wake follows with no edit — a stale run is `unread` before the conclusion is read, and `harness/ciLane.ts:197` keys liveness on `failing`.
